title: Police search for clues to deadly shooting at Oregon elementary school
summary: Schools closed after one teacher and three children killed, and child and teacher hospitalized with critical injuries

blocks.text: Police are investigating a deadly shooting at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, where a 16-year-old opened fire on Thursday, killing three children and a teacher, before being shot dead by an armed bystander.

Authorities in Oregon said that the three children killed at Silver Rail elementary school were aged five, eight and 11, and that a seven-year-old child and a 54-year-old teacher were also hospitalized with critical injuries.
Officials said on Thursday that the gunman was a 16-year-old resident of Bend and that he forced his way into the school at about 1pm by shooting at locked doors.
As of Friday morning, authorities have not named the victims, the shooter or the bystander who shot and killed him. Bend police said the families of the victims had been notified.

Though a suspect has not been formally announced, news outlets including NBC News, the Washington Post and the New York Times, reported that 16-year-old John J Griffin II had been identified as the shooter, citing law enforcement sources.

The Bend police chief, Mike Krantz, said on Thursday that the police received an emergency call at 12.59pm on Thursday from a person “in a vehicle who reported being shot at multiple times by a person with a long gun”.
Within minutes, he said authorities received “dozens of 911 calls” reporting that a “shooter had entered the building at Silver Rail elementary school”.
He said that the school went into lockdown at 1.01pm and that at 1.02pm, the first officers arrived on scene.

“Moments later, an officer reported that the suspect had been shot by a community member who had seen the suspect enter the school and pursued him into the school and engaged him.” Krantz said, adding: “Our officers entered the building and confirmed the suspect was dead.
“They cleared the school to ensure there were no additional threats and then rendered emergency aid to the victims.”
He said officers at the scene then subsequently located “five people who had succumbed to their injuries, including the suspect”.
“This is going to be a long investigation,” he said, adding that the police would maintain a large presence at the school for the next few days.

blocks.caption: Children draw with chalk during a candlelight vigil in Bend on Thursday. Photograph: Eli Imadali/Oregon Public Broadcasting/AP

blocks.text: “There are not really any words I can say to any of you that will make this better,” Krantz said. “But please know that we are working hard to ensure that we conduct a thorough investigation.”
The FBI director, Kash Patel, said the FBI’s local office was on the scene and assisting local law enforcement with the investigation.
The Associated Press, citing a law enforcement official briefed on the shooting who spoke on the condition of anonymity, reported that the shooter used a pump-action shotgun purchased by his mother.
The shooting in Bend is the most deadly school since the September 2024 mass killing at Apalachee high school in Georgia. A 14-year-old shooter killed two teachers and two students.
Although a motive in this school shooting remains unclear, the age of the shooter points to a troubling pattern.

Some of the most recent high-profile shootings on and off school campuses have been carried out by teenagers and young adults, many of whom are a part of nihilistic online communities where posters praise, and seek to emulate, prior shooters like those who have carried out attacks at Columbine high school, in Christchurch in New Zealand, and at Virginia Tech.

In May, two teenagers who met and were radicalized online shot and killed three people at a mosque in San Diego before shooting themselves. In their manifesto, they explicitly name these shooters as their inspiration.
At the news conference on Thursday, the mayor of Bend, Melanie Kebler, said: “Like so many in our community, I’m struggling to make sense of a loss that feels unimaginable.”
Oregon’s governor, Tina Kotek, also attended the conference.

“My heart is absolutely broken today, and our hearts will stay broken in the days and weeks ahead, and my daily prayers will be with this community, with the children, with the parents, and with the educators,” she said.

blocks.caption: A woman cries during a vigil for the victims in Bend on Thursday evening. Photograph: Eli Imadali/Oregon Public Broadcasting/AP

blocks.text: “All Oregonians mourn this loss today,” Kotek added. “This is a horrible day.”
She also praised the person who “heroically intervened to stop further loss of life”.
“Your actions carry a heavy emotional burden, and I just want you to know that my thoughts are with you as well,” she said.

The city of Bend, home to about 100,000 residents, held a candlelit vigil on Thursday night. Hundreds of people gathered in gathered in Bend’s Drake Park as the sun set. Kotek and Kebler attended the vigil.

“There is power and love in this park tonight,” Kotek said. “On behalf of everyone who lives in Oregon, I am so sorry for what you are experiencing today. No parent, no family, no community should have to have this kind of day.”
All schools in Bend and La Pine, a neighboring city, were closed on Friday.
Memorials with flowers, balloons and stuffed animals popped up around the school, which sits in a densely packed neighborhood filled with newly built homes.
Brooke Olsen, whose daughter is a kindergartener at Silver Rail, said she was amazed that a member of the public pursued the shooter.
“I think it’s miraculous that someone was there before law enforcement even arrived to stop further tragedy from happening,” Olsen said on Friday, weeping at times. “I’m feeling very grateful.”
In a statement, Steven Cook, the superintendent of Bend-La Pine schools, said: “We are stunned and heartbroken by this senseless tragedy.
“We extend our deepest sympathy to the families and to everyone affected by this violence,” Cook said. “No words can adequately express the grief our community is experiencing.”

The US education secretary, Linda McMahon, also expressed her condolences in a social media post on Thursday, saying that she was “heartbroken by the horrific shooting” and that her “prayers are with the students, faculty, their families, and the entire community”.
The Associated Press contributed reporting
